citations.title: Single-cell RNA-seq reveals the diversity of trophoblast subtypes and patterns of differentiation in the human placenta
citations.authors: Liu Y, Fan X, Wang R, et al.
citations.evidence: scRNA-seq of first/second-trimester villi identifies CTB, EVT, STB, Hofbauer and mesenchymal stromal cells; villous cytotrophoblast is the dominant trophoblast compartment and is proliferative (Ki67+ at villous CTB and cell-column base).

citations.title: Single-cell reconstruction of the early maternal-fetal interface in humans
citations.authors: Vento-Tormo R, Efremova M, Botting RA, et al.
citations.evidence: First-trimester maternal-fetal interface atlas confirms the villous cytotrophoblast (VCT) as the proliferative trophoblast stem pool, the largest trophoblast population in early placenta.

notes: Directionally correct: VCT/CTB is the proliferative stem pool and the dominant trophoblast type in first-trimester villi, so its being the single largest annotated population is biologically plausible. Caveat: the exact 0.40 fraction is an artifact of this dissociated, multi-study, HVG-subset dataset and its annotation scheme, NOT a true tissue proportion. The HumRepUpdate 2024 meta-analysis notes trophoblasts span 20-42% of captured cells depending heavily on dissociation protocol and sampling site; enzymatic dissociation systematically biases cell-type proportions. Also note STB is heavily under-recovered in scRNA-seq (multinucleate, lost on dissociation), so 'CTB largest' partly reflects STB drop-out, not just CTB abundance.

citations.title: Single-cell reconstruction of the early maternal-fetal interface in humans
citations.authors: Vento-Tormo R, Efremova M, Botting RA, et al.
citations.evidence: Identifies perivascular cells (PV1, PV2) as a distinct mural/vascular-associated mesenchymal compartment sharing the smooth-muscle marker MGP and distinguished by MCAM/MMP11, i.e. a subset carved out of the broader stromal/mesenchymal population.

citations.title: Revealing the molecular landscape of human placenta: a systematic review and meta-analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing studies
citations.evidence: Notes perivascular cells as a stromal compartment whose recognition depends on annotation resolution; nomenclature and whether they are split out of stroma varies across studies.

notes: Supported as a methodological/annotation statement: perivascular (pericyte/mural) cells are genuinely a vascular-associated subset of the mesenchymal/stromal compartment, so splitting them out of 'Stroma' under a finer annotation column and thereby lowering the stromal fraction is exactly what one expects. Caveat: 'perivascular' here means pericyte/mural cells (MGP/MCAM/ACTA2/PDGFRB/RGS5-type identity), which are vascular wall cells rather than fibroblastic villous stroma proper; lumping them under 'Stroma' in the coarse scheme is a simplification. The fraction change is purely a labeling-granularity effect, not a biological change in the tissue.

citations.title: Revealing the molecular landscape of human placenta: a systematic review and meta-analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing studies
citations.evidence: Across placenta scRNA-seq studies, trophoblasts comprise 20-42% of captured cells regardless of gestational age, with stromal and Hofbauer/macrophage populations consistently among the major compartments; proportions vary strongly with method.

citations.title: Single-cell RNA-seq reveals the diversity of trophoblast subtypes and patterns of differentiation in the human placenta
citations.authors: Liu Y, Fan X, Wang R, et al.
citations.evidence: Five major placental compartments recovered by scRNA-seq: trophoblast (CTB/EVT/STB), stromal/mesenchymal, Hofbauer macrophages, endothelial, and antigen-presenting cells - the same scheme as the term dataset here.

notes: Supported that term placenta scRNA-seq is dominated by trophoblast (CTB), stroma and Hofbauer cells with smaller EVT/STB/endothelial/perivascular fractions - this matches the recognized compartment list and the ~20-42% trophoblast range. Caveat: the precise term fractions (CTB 0.33, stroma 0.28, Hofbauer 0.25) are dataset- and dissociation-specific, not canonical tissue proportions; the meta-analysis explicitly warns that proportions track methodology (dissociation, sampling site, sorting) more than biology. The unusually high Hofbauer fraction in particular is suspect (see claim-shift-direction).

citations.title: Cytotrophoblast Layer of Human Chorionic Villi Becomes Thinner but Maintains Its Structural Integrity During Gestation
citations.evidence: The villous cytotrophoblast layer thins and becomes discontinuous from first trimester to term (continuity ~90% first trimester vs ~80% term), consistent with a declining relative CTB contribution as villi mature.

citations.title: Gestational Dynamics of Hofbauer Cells in the Human Placenta: Distribution, Morphology, and Immunophenotype
citations.evidence: Hofbauer cell numerical density peaks in the second trimester and is LOWEST in the third trimester/term (proliferative index ~82% first trimester, absent by third trimester) - i.e. HC density tends to fall, not rise, toward term.

citations.title: Gestational age-dependent decrease in fetal Hofbauer cells in placentas from pregnancies exposed to wildfire smoke in California
citations.evidence: In unexposed control placentas, villous Hofbauer cell density was NOT significantly associated with gestational age - i.e. no robust HC increase toward term.

citations.title: Revealing the molecular landscape of human placenta: a systematic review and meta-analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing studies
citations.evidence: Reported scRNA-seq cell-type proportions vary widely and track dissociation protocol, sampling site and sorting more than gestational biology; trophoblast fraction (20-42%) is not consistently gestation-dependent.

notes: Split verdict. The CTB-falls direction is biologically defensible (villous cytotrophoblast layer thins/becomes discontinuous toward term). But the headline 'Hofbauer macrophage compartment expands toward term' is NOT supported and is arguably refuted by histology: morphometric studies find Hofbauer cell density peaks in the second trimester and DECLINES toward term, and a controlled study found no gestational-age association in unexposed placentas. The scRNA-seq Hofbauer fraction rising from 0.16 to 0.25 most likely reflects cross-dataset dissociation/sorting/annotation differences (macrophages survive dissociation well; multinucleate STB is lost) rather than a true increase in placental macrophages. These are TWO different studies/protocols compared cross-sectionally, not a matched gestational time course, so the 'maturation' interpretation conflates batch/method effects with development. Treat the directional shift as method-confounded, not established placental biology.

citations.title: Single-cell RNA-seq reveals the diversity of trophoblast subtypes and patterns of differentiation in the human placenta
citations.authors: Liu Y, Fan X, Wang R, et al.
citations.evidence: Establishes the standard placental villous compartments: trophoblast (CTB/EVT/STB), stromal/mesenchymal, Hofbauer macrophages, endothelial - the recurrent annotation scheme used across placenta scRNA-seq.

citations.title: Single-cell reconstruction of the early maternal-fetal interface in humans
citations.authors: Vento-Tormo R, Efremova M, Botting RA, et al.
citations.evidence: Defines perivascular (PV1/PV2) cells, endothelial cells, and the trophoblast lineage at the maternal-fetal interface, corroborating each label in the shared 7-compartment set as a recognized placental cell identity.

citations.title: The Elusive Role of Placental Macrophages: The Hofbauer Cell
citations.evidence: Confirms Hofbauer cells are fetal-origin resident placental macrophages in the villous mesenchymal/stromal core.

notes: The seven labels (CTB, STB, EVT, Hofbauer cells, Endothelial, Perivascular, Stroma) are each genuine, well-characterized placental compartments, so harmonizing them onto a common scheme is biologically legitimate. Caveats: (1) sharing label STRINGS does not guarantee the underlying cell populations were defined by the same markers/thresholds - the HumRepUpdate 2024 meta-analysis stresses no marker is shared across studies for any cell type, so a 'CTB' in one atlas may be delineated differently from 'CTB' in the other; (2) the coarse scheme hides biologically real subtype shifts (e.g. EVT and STB subsets, Hofbauer M1/M2 states) and folds pericytes/perivascular distinctly only when annotation resolution allows. Label-set identity is necessary but not sufficient for a clean cross-atlas comparison.

citations.title: Orchestrating single-cell analysis with Bioconductor / current best practices in scRNA-seq normalization
citations.evidence: Standard scRNA-seq practice: store raw integer UMI counts in a dedicated layer and a log1p size-factor-normalized matrix in X; raw counts are required for re-normalization, model-based DE and pseudobulk.

notes: This is a data-provenance/processing assertion with low biological content, judged on convention rather than placental biology. The convention it invokes is correct: integer UMI counts (min 0, no negatives, all integers) are the raw count representation, and a log1p matrix matching layers['log1pM'] is normalized; raw counts being present does make re-normalization/pseudobulk recoverable. Caveat: literature review cannot itself verify the numeric integer/non-integer checks on these specific files - that is the numeric reviewer's job; I only affirm the stated interpretation is consistent with standard AnnData conventions. 'Suitable for pseudobulk' also assumes the counts are true per-cell UMIs and not, e.g., already ambient-corrected/scaled, which the data state alone cannot fully guarantee.

citations.title: Orchestrating single-cell analysis with Bioconductor / current best practices in scRNA-seq normalization
citations.evidence: Count-based DE/pseudobulk methods (e.g. negative-binomial models) require genuine integer counts; a non-integer 'counts' layer (log/normalized values) cannot be used as input and indicates the raw counts were not retained.

notes: Data-provenance assertion, low biological content - judged on bioinformatic convention. The interpretation is sound: if X, layers['counts'] and raw.X are all non-integer/non-negative, then no genuine raw counts survive, the 'counts' layer is misnamed, and count-model DE/pseudobulk cannot be run directly on first trimester; thus the two datasets are asymmetric in available raw data, which is a real and important cross-dataset caveat. Caveats: (1) literature review does not re-verify the numeric integer-fraction checks (numeric reviewer's track); (2) non-integerness alone does not prove counts are unrecoverable in principle - sometimes raw counts exist elsewhere (a separate file/GEO deposit) even if absent from this h5ad; the claim is correct as stated only about THIS object.

citations.title: Revealing the molecular landscape of human placenta: a systematic review and meta-analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing studies
citations.evidence: Placenta scRNA-seq atlases are routinely integrated across multiple studies/donors and reported cell-type proportions are strongly influenced by donor, dissociation protocol and sampling site - i.e. pooled fractions are not per-donor and carry between-study batch structure.

citations.title: Systematic assessment of tissue dissociation and storage biases in single-cell and single-nucleus RNA-seq workflows
citations.evidence: Dissociation protocol and processing systematically alter recovered cell-type proportions, so pooling across studies/protocols confounds composition - the rationale for treating pooled fractions cautiously.

notes: The interpretation - both are multi-study integrated atlases whose cell-type fractions are pooled across donors/studies rather than per-donor - is correct and methodologically important. Caveat: with cell-type fractions pooled over only 3 studies (and term having NaN sample_id for 8321 cells), donor- and study-level batch effects are confounded with any apparent gestational difference; no per-donor variance or statistics can be derived from pooled fractions, so cross-dataset composition deltas should not be over-interpreted. Largely a study-design/batch statement with low intrinsic biological content.

citations.title: Selecting highly variable genes / current best practices in single-cell RNA-seq analysis
citations.evidence: Standard scRNA-seq workflows subset to ~1000-5000 highly variable genes for the working/embedding matrix while retaining the full gene set in raw, exactly the structure described.

notes: This is a dataset-shape/processing description (cell and gene counts, HVG subsetting), not a biological claim, so there is essentially nothing in the published literature to confirm or refute - hence 'uncertain' at low confidence on biological grounds. The only literature-anchored element is that reducing to a 5000-gene HVG working matrix is a conventional, accepted scRNA-seq step. The numeric facts (35461 cells, 5000 genes, 27526 raw) are for the numeric reviewer to verify; I do not affirm them. 'Larger dataset by cell count' is a within-this-comparison statement, not a general property of first-trimester placenta.

citations.title: Selecting highly variable genes / current best practices in single-cell RNA-seq analysis
citations.evidence: Retaining the full ~20-30k gene set in X (no HVG subsetting of var) is a valid, common scRNA-seq object configuration; absence of adata.raw is a storage choice, not a biological property.

notes: Pure object-shape/processing description (23378 cells, 25777 genes, raw is None, fewer cells than FT) with no biological content to test against the literature - 'uncertain' at low confidence accordingly. It is conventional and unremarkable for one atlas to keep the full gene set while another is HVG-subset. The cell/gene counts are the numeric reviewer's to verify; 'fewer cells than first trimester' is specific to this pair of files and implies nothing about term placenta in general.

citations.title: Microbiome Datasets Are Compositional: And This Is Not Optional
citations.authors: Gloor GB, Macklaim JM, Pawlowsky-Glahn V, Egozcue JJ.
citations.evidence: Proportions constrained to sum to 1 (simplex/closure) are compositional: an increase in one component forces a decrease in others, so apparent changes are relative redistributions, not absolute changes - the principle this claim invokes.

notes: A mathematical/compositional statement (fractions sum to 1, deltas sum to ~0, so the shift is a redistribution), not a biological claim - so literature can only affirm the underlying statistics, not any placental biology. The interpretation is correct and is in fact an essential caveat for claim-shift-direction: because the data are compositional, a 'rise' in Hofbauer/stroma fraction is partly forced by a fall elsewhere (e.g. CTB), and cannot be read as an absolute increase in macrophage numbers in the tissue. Confidence low on biological substance; the arithmetic itself is the numeric reviewer's domain.

citations.title: Revealing the molecular landscape of human placenta: a systematic review and meta-analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing studies
citations.evidence: Cross-study placenta scRNA-seq comparisons are hampered by differing gene annotations/feature sets and marker usage; harmonizing on a shared/full gene namespace is the recommended basis for cross-atlas gene-level analysis.

notes: A bioinformatic feature-space statement (HVG vs full-gene overlap, Jaccard) with no placental biology to verify - 'uncertain' on biological grounds. The interpretation is methodologically sensible: HVG-subset overlap is small because one set is reduced to 5000 genes, and cross-dataset gene-level work should use the raw/full namespaces (~18480 shared, Jaccard 0.53). Caveat: even the 'full' overlap is incomplete (different reference builds/feature filtering), and gene-symbol-based intersection can miss genuinely shared genes that differ only in symbol/ID version - a real cross-atlas pitfall. Numeric values are the numeric reviewer's to verify.
